subject: Closed-handle value: close() leaves a defined not-writable value behind (buys never-opened-vs-closed distinction)
description:
RULED s338 (fable-answers-s337.md §4): YES, queued BEHIND #153/E4.1.

Today %p-forget-fh leaves the variable UNDEFINED after close(), so `print $closed_fh ...` and `my $u; print {$u} ...` arrive at %p-out-fh-or-fail identical — which is why the "Can't use an undefined value as a symbol reference" die for a never-opened handle was measured-and-reverted in s337c (the measurement is recorded in %p-out-fh-or-fail's docstring; do not retry it without this task).

Fix shape: close() leaves a defined closed-handle value (glob/fh object marked closed). Then:
- undef designator -> die "Can't use an undefined value as a symbol reference" (perl-correct);
- closed handle -> current behavior (EBADF, no output, return false) stays;
- fileno/-t/eof diagnostics on a closed handle become answerable.

Same magic-cell family as #144 (\$! aliasing) — implement with an eye on sharing the mechanism. Interaction: #198 (IO::Handle DESTROY at scope exit) fires on exactly this value, so landing #220 first makes #198 smaller.
